answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it earns reputation, like a jade token bound to one real identity. Think of reputation as an atlas: every deal, review, and payment draws a route on a shared map, and a fake agent with no history has no roads leading anywhere. New agents enter through a single narrow inlet, earning small trust gradually by completing real work for real counterparties, so spawning a thousand empty identities costs more than it can ever return.
